messages:
ashley: quick check-in — on canary we've seen sporadic crashes when the attention kernel touches KV pages that are being compacted/evicted. runtime v1.9 + attn-slab on canaries, stack traces point at stale pointers into page blocks. not a regression in attn math, more a liveness/handle problem.

dan: can you paste the crash snippet? and which eviction path (LRU vs compaction) is doing the free?

ashley: here's the minimal repro log (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-12T15:04:02Z] attn_kernel: begin forward, shard=3, seq=8192
[2026-02-12T15:04:02Z] kv_manager: compacting block=0x7f8b2c, migrating 4 slots
[2026-02-12T15:04:02Z] attn_kernel: load_kv_block ptr=0x7f8b2c->0x0 (use-after-free)
SIGSEGV at 0x7f8b2c
```
looks like compaction is moving pages under kernels that still hold raw pointers to block memory.

priya: that matches my local stress run. fragmentation + background compaction means we sometimes relocate backing memory while the kernel still holds a direct pointer into the slab. we need either pinning or an indirection layer.

marc: curious about cost. naive pinning (prevent free/move while in-flight) adds headroom overhead. did you benchmark impact vs crash frequency?

ashley: rough numbers from canary:
- baseline (no pin): crash ~ 1/10k long requests
- with coarse pin-by-block: crash ~ 0, mem overhead +6% under loaded batch
- latency tail + ~5% p95 on long contexts (seq>6k)

priya: proposal: introduce ephemeral page_handle that the kernel references instead of raw ptrs. page_handle is small (8B) and contains an epoch+slot index. KV manager updates an indirection table on compaction. semantics:
- kernel calls `acquire_page(handle)` at request start -> returns mapped pointer or RETRY
- on compaction, manager atomically updates indirection and increments epoch; old physical memory is only reclaimed after epoch drain
- fast path inline for common case (handle resolves to same ptr)

ashley: pseudo-ABI sketch:
```
struct page_handle { u32 slot_idx; u32 epoch; };
ptr = resolve(handle);
if (ptr == NULL) return RETRY; // kernel retries or falls back to smaller context
```
this keeps kernel cheap but safe.

dan: sounds good. two questions: (1) where do we stash indirections—per-shard array or global? (2) how to minimize resolves per token to avoid perf tax?

priya: per-shard indirection gives locality; we can cache resolved ptrs in the kernel per-request and only re-resolve on kernel start or on a short periodic check. also expose a `resolve_hint` that is a cached ptr + epoch, so common case is just a pointer + epoch compare.

marc: fallback plan if resolve fails during mid-attention? Do we restart from earlier kv depth or fallback to smaller model variant?

ashley: current idea — kernel returns a transient RETRY code. serving runtime does quick policy: if retry_count < 2 -> try again (likely compaction finished), else route to compatible model variant (quant/half precision) or return a graceful 503 to caller depending on customer SLA.

infra-bot: rollout note: deployed epochal-handle support to canary hosts (rg-10), metric kv_handle_retries is emitting ~0.3% spikes during compaction windows. no crashes observed since 2026-02-12T16:00Z.

dan: next steps: we need a tiny RFC to pin down ABI, fallback semantics, and a benchmark harness that exercises heavy fragmentation. priya, can you prototype the indirection table and a resolve_hint fast-path?

priya: yep, I'll draft a follow-up RFC and a microbenchmark that simulates migrating 100k small slots under high concurrent kernel load. aim to get PR in 2 weeks.

marc: ack. I'll model the cost (p95 tail, mem overhead) and add a cost-awareness knob to autoscaler to tolerate the pin headroom when enabled.

ashley: sweet — I'll update the canary job to enable the resolve_hint and collect per-request resolve counts. ping me when the RFC is up and we'll slot this for arhitecture sync next Tues. :thumbsup:
